Forecast Discussion

High pressure over New England slides offshore today. An east wind brings thicker clouds and much more humid air.

Low pressure moves north from Florida through the Carolinas tonight and Sunday. Rain develops from south to north this evening and increases after midnight. Rain continues Sunday morning, steadiest along the Blue Ridge, then tapers off in the afternoon as the low pulls away.

A cold front crosses from the west Monday morning. A few showers come with it along the western escarpment. Northwest winds turn breezy behind the front in the afternoon.

Tuesday is dry and cooler as high pressure builds across the Midwest.

That high shifts to New England Tuesday night. Cold air wedges down the east side of the Appalachians Wednesday while low pressure develops along the Gulf coast. Rain develops Wednesday afternoon and continues Wednesday night. The highest elevations may mix with snow at times, but we expect no accumulation.

The low moves up the Carolina coast Thanksgiving Day. Rain tapers off in the afternoon, lingering longest along the western escarpment. Colder air follows in the evening, and a few rain or snow showers may mix at higher elevations.

Friday is dry and cold as high pressure builds in from the west.
